## 10. Terminology findings

| Term | Hits | Files | Proposed | Automatic? |
|---|---:|---:|---|---|
| "5 Pillars" / "Five Pillars" | 23 | 7 | "Five Foundations" | **Yes** |
| bare "pillar" / "pillars" | 68 | 11 | "foundation(s)" | **No** |
| EECA | 20 | 6 | per-market equivalent | **No** |
| litres | 41 | 7 | gallons for the US | **No** |
| Healthy Homes | 7 | 2 | per-market equivalent | **No** |
| R-values | 6 | 1 | per-market equivalent | **No** |
| Civil Defence | 1 | 1 | SES (AU) / emergency management (US, CA) | **No** |
| NZ agencies (MBIE, WINZ, ACC…) | 2 | 1 | per-market equivalent | **No** |

### Terminology that must NOT be changed automatically

- **Bare "pillar"** — two of these documents also discuss building structure, where a pillar is a literal
  pillar holding up a literal house. A global find-and-replace would produce nonsense in exactly the
  documents where accuracy matters most.
- **Every country-specific term.** The library serves NZ, AU, US and CA. EECA, Healthy Homes, Civil Defence
  and R-values are not outdated wording to be corrected — they are **New Zealand content that needs per-market
  variants**. "litres" likewise: the US needs gallons.

## 10b. Content and safety gaps — the finding I did not expect

These are not branding problems, and they are the main reason 34 resources are in migration group B rather
than A:

1. **No emergency number appears anywhere in the programme.** Not one of the 90 files tells a member which
   number to ring — including OG-06, the 72-Hour Emergency Checklist. This needs a per-market answer
   (NZ 111, AU 000, US and CA 911). For a household resilience programme, this is the gap I would fix first.
2. **Batteries and inverters are taught without a licensed-electrician warning** — 11 resources including
   OG-18 Solar Power 101 Workbook and OG-21.
3. **Stored drinking water is covered without a potability or treatment warning** — 8 resources including
   OG-09 and OG-10.
4. **Solid fuel heating is covered without a flue maintenance or clearance warning** — 7 resources including
   OG-17 Solid Fuel Heating Planner.
5. **Gas appliances are covered without a ventilation or certified-installer warning.**

A passing mention does not count: a topic must be returned to at least three times before it is treated as
taught, so a scorecard listing the word "generator" is not flagged.

**There are no disclaimers of any kind in any programme file.**

## 12. Proposed OG code → resource id

`legacyCode` keeps `OG-xx` permanently. The library id follows the library's own `res-0000` format, so the
programme can be renumbered or reordered later without breaking a single link:

| Range | Mapping |
|---|---|
| Core | OG-01 → `res-1001` … OG-30 → `res-1030` |
| Bonus | OG-B01 → `res-1501` … OG-B15 → `res-1515` |

All 45 are unique, all match the library's id format, and core and bonus ranges are kept apart with room
between them. The complete table, with proposed slugs, is section 12 of the detailed report.

## 15. Owner decisions required

1. **Safety wording — my recommendation is to treat this as blocking.** The programme teaches generators,
   solid fuel heating, gas, batteries and stored drinking water with no warnings and no disclaimers, and gives
   no emergency number. I would write the safety and emergency wording *before* re-skinning, not after:
   re-skinning first means doing the layout work twice. Do you want Stage 9.6 to draft that wording for your
   approval?
2. **Market variants.** 8 kinds of NZ-specific content (EECA, Healthy Homes, Civil Defence, litres, R-values,
   NZ agencies). Options: ship NZ-first and mark the rest "NZ-specific"; write four variants; or neutralise
   the wording. This decision changes the size of the re-skin substantially.
3. **Air has one resource out of 45.** Air is one of the Five Foundations but has only OG-13. Is that
   deliberate for this programme, or a gap to fill before the library launches?
4. **The 6 unresolved types** (OG-20, OG-22, OG-28, OG-B05, OG-B11, OG-B15) need your call, or mine on your
   instruction. My reading: OG-28 Household Responsibility Roster and OG-B15 Annual Maintenance Calendar are
   Templates; OG-22 Resilience Product Wishlist is a Worksheet; OG-20 Alternative Energy Suitability Check is
   an Assessment; OG-B05 Community Call Prep Sheet is a Template; OG-B11 Building Consent Navigator is a Guide.
5. **Confirm the id scheme** (`res-1001…1030`, `res-1501…1515`) before anything is built on it.
6. **Bonus resource placement.** All 15 audited as ordinary library resources. Confirm whether they should
   appear as a distinct "bonus" collection, or simply as library resources with no special status.

---

## 16. Recommendation for Stage 9.6

Stage 9.6 was planned as final QC. Given what this audit found, I recommend reshaping it:

1. **Safety and disclaimer wording first** — draft the warnings and the per-market emergency guidance for your
   approval. It is the only finding here with real-world consequences, and it is cheap to fix before layout.
2. **Then the market-variant decision** (§15.2), because it determines how much copy the re-skin touches.
3. **Then re-skin group A** — 11 resources, presentation only, lowest risk. That proves the re-skin pipeline
   end to end on the easy cases before committing to the other 34.
4. **Then final QC** as originally planned, and only then real importing.

I would not enable `--real` until at least group A has been re-skinned and one resource has gone through the
whole chain — re-skin, import, appear in the library — on a private deployment.
